caption: What if you lived one year in one of the wettest places on Earth? Mawsynram in Meghalaya averages about 11,870 mm of rain a year, and Guinness lists it for the highest average annual rainfall. Delhi's long-term average is about 774 mm, so that's roughly 15 times more. If none of it drained away, a year's rain would stand nearly 12 metres deep. June and July each bring over 3 metres. Khasi farmers wear the knup, a bamboo rain shield that keeps both hands free, and villages here grow living root bridges that can last for centuries. Nearby Cherrapunji (Sohra) holds the 12-month record: 26,461 mm from August 1860 to July 1861. Yet December averages only about 4 mm, and Sohra has faced drinking-water shortages in the dry season. Could YOU survive a year of rain? 👇
